title.narrative: FSDZ Kvinnor & ungdomar i finansiell inkludering WIN 2
FSDZ Women & Youth in Financial Inclusion WIN 2

description.narrative: The WIN 2 programme will contribute to systemic and lasting change, particularly benefiting poor women, youth, and the disabled, through a market systems development approach to financial inclusion and addressing of financial barriers to real sector engagement. The three key work areas are: 1) digitization for financial inclusion, with the aim of reducing transaction costs and increasing market information flows in terms of time and money for poor women, youth, people with disabilities, and their households; 2) financial education, with the aim of improving life conditions of poor women, youth, people with disabilities and their households through improved financial capabilities, leading to improved access to income opportunities, social welfare, basic health and education services; and 3) women and youth savings groups, with the aim of creating agency for women, youth and people with disabilities to improve sustainable income flows, access social services for them and their families, voice opinion and take leadership, as well as enabling increased financial inclusion.

The WIN 2 programme is implemented by Financial Sector Deepening Zambia and is based on lessons learned from the WIN project (June 2016 - February 2020). The time frame for the WIN 2 programme is 2020 to 2025, and the overall budget is SEK 40 million.
The WIN 2 programme will promote greater financial inclusion and capabilities for women, youth, people with disabilities, and their households. The three key work areas are: 1) digitization for financial inclusion; 2) financial education; and 3) women and youth savings groups.
Financial Sector Deepening Zambia will implement this programme together with the Government of Zambia and a number of civil society and private sector partners. Some of the funds will be forwarded to some of these partners.

WIN 2-programmet implementeras av Financial Sector Deepening Zambia och bygger på lärdomar från WIN-projektet (juni 2016 - februari 2020). Tidsramen för WIN 2-programmet är 2020 till 2025 och den totala budgeten är 40 miljoner SEK.
WIN 2-programmet kommer att främja ökad finansiell inkludering och kapacitet för kvinnor, ungdomar, personer med funktionsnedsättning och deras hushåll. De tre viktigaste arbetsområdena är: 1) digitalisering för finansiell integration; 2) finansiell utbildning; och 3) kvinnor och ungdomsbesparingsgrupper.
Financial Sector Deepening Zambia kommer att genomföra detta program tillsammans med Zambias regering och ett antal civilsamhällets organisationer och privata partner. En del av medlen kommer att vidarebefordras till några av dessa partner.

title.narrative: Decision on Contribution FSDZ WIN II

description.narrative:
FSD Zambia in collaboration with the University of Nottingham and the African Studies Centre Leiden University completed their analysis and hosted a Gender and Social Norms Study Results Dissemination Meeting. With support from the Embassy of Sweden and the FSD Network Gender CoPro, the unique and groundbreaking studies provided very important information and lessons about how husbands and wives respond very differently in society and with each other on savings, use, and sharing of money.
Cheshire Homes Society of Zambia (CHSZ) is implementing Financial Education for Women, Youth, and People with disabilities in Eastern Province. The CHSZ project team formed and monitors 47 financial education (FE) Clubs from 27 schools to support progress and help address the challenges that the different schools are facing in running FE clubs. Most schools reported some challenges with access to necessary materials that would aid them in conducting activities in the FE Clubs, such as standard registers, lesson plan templates, and action plans. The project has reached a total of 980 caregivers (834F, 146M) of children with disabilities. A total of 514 children with disabilities, out of which 200 with physical disabilities had parents in savings groups with 44 savings groups having been validated as functional.
Impact Hub has been implementing the Financial Education for Economic Transformation (FEET) project in TVET institutions in Lusaka and the Copperbelt, targeted at young women, men, and youth with disabilities aged between 15 and 35. The rollouts in the year has yielded a total of 1,698 (890F, 808M) students who have undergone the financial education course, a 48% overachievement against the project target of 4,415. Impact Hub also conducted business proposal writing mentorship classes aimed at empowering students with knowledge and skills on how to put their business ideas, technical and vocational skills into formal documents and structures that are viable and investment ready.
Restless Development has been implementing the Tusunge Lubono (Lets Grow Our Wealth) II project 2022 2025 and are now starting the second year of implementation. The Tusunge Lubono Phase II project is improving the standard of living of women, youth and people with disabilities at a household level in the rural and peri urban areas of Central and Northern Provinces. 41 savings groups have been formed, including 6 couples savings groups. Restless Development has also innovated and began employing SAVIX MIS a digital Savings Groups Information Exchange Management Information System to manage SG data.
Barefeet Theatre has been working to provide financial education to children with disabilities through the Theatre for Development (T4D) approach and help the to form savings gropus among persons with physical disabilities as well as those without them, to help both groups transition from vulnerability. The project has reached out to 300 participants and has formed 10 savings groups.
